subject.title: [Bug]: browser navigation-guard explicit hostname allowlist broken by SSRF loopback tightening (#100835)

question: Should browser navigation allowlists permit non-localhost hostnames that resolve to loopback after the trusted-host SSRF hardening, and if so should metadata/link-local DNS answers still stay blocked?
rationale: The current behavior is a security-boundary tradeoff between operator-declared browser exceptions and the merged DNS-rebinding hardening; automation should not choose that policy for maintainers.

options.title: Allow only scoped loopback aliases
options.body: Approve a narrowed browser fix that permits the explicit loopback-resolution case while preserving metadata/link-local DNS-answer blocking and adding proof.

options.title: Keep the hardened SSRF behavior
options.body: Retire the old navigation test contract and update docs/tests so only localhost, loopback literals, or explicit private-network opt-in allow loopback targets.

options.title: Pause for broader policy design
options.body: Leave this issue open until browser navigation, CDP control, and shared SSRF allowlist semantics are redesigned together.

recommendation.title: Allow only scoped loopback aliases
recommendation.body: Approve a narrowed browser fix that permits the explicit loopback-resolution case while preserving metadata/link-local DNS-answer blocking and adding proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They opened the canonical issue and merged the related SSRF hardening PR, making them the strongest available owner for the contract decision.
